walkthroughs.body_html:
Liquids can't be squashed, so they transmit pressure perfectly.

Push a small piston with a tiny force - it creates pressure in the liquid - which lifts a giant piston with a huge force.

That's how a tiny car brake pedal stops a heavy car, and how hydraulic lifts can raise tons!

For weird shapes (like a stone), use displacement:

1. Fill a measuring cylinder with water.
2. Note the level.
3. Drop the object in.
4. Read the new level.
5. Difference = the object's volume.

Now find mass with a balance and calculate density!

A barometer measures air pressure.

High pressure = settled, sunny weather.
Low pressure = clouds, rain, storms.

Weather forecasters watch pressure maps to predict storms days ahead.

mcqs.q: What property of a sound wave determines its pitch?
options: Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
Amplitude determines pitch — a bigger wave is a higher-pitched note.
The frequency — higher frequency means higher pitch.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.

mcqs.q: Is radioactive decay periodic — does each nucleus decay at regular intervals?
options: No — decay is a random process; half-life is a statistical property of a large population.
The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
Yes — half-life is the time between each emission from the source.
Yes — each nucleus 'ticks' at intervals of one half-life until it decays.

mcqs.q: What absorber is needed to stop beta radiation?
options: The speed of the wave determines pitch — faster waves sound higher.
Thick lead — only lead can stop any radiation.
A few millimetres of aluminium (or similar thin metal sheet).
A sheet of paper — beta is only slightly more penetrating than alpha.
